This is a great book that doesn't just preach but it does give clear guidelines. It basically puts it in English what it takes to be a writer.
Words For Pictures by Brian Michael Bendis is a book about writing for comic books. It's incredibly informative and fun to read.
Understanding Comics by Scott McCloud is an excellent comic book about comic books.
The follow-up "Making Comics" explains a lot of theory for making a good comic, too.
Libromancer is a book about a wizard who can pull objects out of books. Can't think of the author's name, but the story reads similar to the Dresden Files, if there are any fans of those here.

The Shadow of the Wind by Carlos Ruiz Zafon. Set in Barcelona and THe main character works in a bookstore and is invited to visit the Cemetery of Forgotten Books. The Angel's Game is a continuation of the story. Excellent reads.
The "Thursday Next" series of detective novels are great for people who geek out about books.
The Rule of Four is decent, if a little slow paced at times. The events in the story revolve around a university student's work decoding the Hypnerotomachia Poliphili.
If on a Winter's Night a Traveler by Italo Calvino
Not sure it quite fits what you're after but House of Leaves was a wonderful read!

On Writing and The Joy of Reading. On Writing is Kings best work to date. Honest and on point and clearly shows he knows what he's doing as both a writer and a former English teacher. Charles Van Doren's book the Joy of Reading is also a fine book , but his book A Brief History of Knowledge trumps it handily.
